Use cases

How teams use Connectora for LinkedIn outreach

Connectora was built inside a growth agency that runs LinkedIn outreach every day. These are the setups we see work, by type of team.

Book a demo
TeamTypical setupMost-used features
AgenciesSeveral client campaigns, many sender accountsMulti-account sending, campaign filters in the Unibox, CRM webhooks
B2B sales and SDR teamsOne campaign per segment, reps' accounts pooledPooled limits, private inboxes, AI reply drafts

Agencies

How do agencies use Connectora to run LinkedIn outreach for clients?

Agencies run a separate Connectora campaign for each client and segment, sending from the LinkedIn accounts assigned to that client. Each account's daily limit is shared across campaigns, so no profile is overloaded. Replies land in one Unibox that can be filtered by campaign, and signed webhooks push them into each client's CRM.

Agency

Example setup

  • Campaign naming by client, market and segment, for example CLIENT-UAE-D2C-FASHION.
  • Senders: the client's team accounts, or the agency's own accounts where the client agrees.
  • Schedule in the prospects' timezone, for example 08:00 to 18:30, Monday to Friday.
  • Sequence: connection request with a short note → message after 1 hour to 1 day → two follow-ups 2 to 3 days apart.
  • Unibox filtered by campaign for each client's daily reply review.
Why it fits: a queue that explains itself ("147 from next week") makes client reporting simple, and the funnel gives acceptance and reply rates per campaign without spreadsheets.

PlanMost agencies fit the Agency plan (11 to 50 accounts) at $18 per account a month, white-label included. See pricing.

Sales and SDR teams

How do B2B sales and SDR teams use Connectora?

Sales teams connect each rep's LinkedIn account and run shared campaigns by segment. Connectora spreads leads across reps according to each account's remaining capacity, keeps every rep's personal chats private, and routes outreach replies to one inbox where AI drafts help reps answer quickly and consistently.

Sales team

Example setup

  • One campaign per segment or territory; each rep's account as a sender.
  • Daily limits set per rep based on each account's safety score.
  • Reply handling: reps filter the Unibox by their own account; managers filter by campaign.
  • CRM: a webhook sends every reply, with history, to your CRM via Zapier or Make.
Why it fits: no rep's profile carries the whole campaign, and a lead is never contacted twice by two reps.

PlanGrowth, $21 per account a month for 3 to 10 accounts.

Founders and consultants

How can founders and consultants use Connectora safely?

Founders and consultants usually connect one or two personal LinkedIn accounts. Connectora's safe defaults (20 requests a day, working hours only, warm-up for new profiles) keep the pace modest, while Hold & Resume and AI drafts make sure every interested reply gets a fast, personal answer from the founder.

Founder

Example setup

  • Sequence: connection request with a personal note → one useful message after acceptance → one follow-up after a week.
  • Limit: start at the default and only raise it if acceptance stays healthy.
  • 15 minutes a day in the Unibox: answer held leads first, use Draft with AI for the rest.
Why it fits: your name is on every message, so pace and tone matter more than volume.

PlanStarter, $24 per account a month for 1 or 2 accounts.

Event and content marketers

How do event and content marketers use post-engager lists?

Event and content teams paste the URL of a webinar, launch or thought-leadership post into Connectora to collect the people who reacted and commented. The resulting list goes into a campaign whose note references the post, which makes the first touch relevant and lifts acceptance compared with cold lists.

Events & content

Example note (under 300 characters)

Hi {firstName}, saw you reacted to our post on [post topic]. I'm connecting with people working on this. Happy to share what we learned from the session.
Why it fits: these prospects have already raised their hand. The job is to follow up quickly, not to convince a stranger.

How to build the list: post-engager sourcing.

Switching tools

How do teams switch to Connectora from another LinkedIn tool?

Teams moving from another LinkedIn automation tool upload their existing lead lists, import live conversations with Import Chat so threads continue in the Unibox, and clear out old pending invitations with Connectora's paced withdrawal queue. Duplicate checks stop anyone already contacted from receiving a second sequence.

Switching

Switching checklist

  1. Export your lead lists from the old tool and upload them; invalid and duplicate rows are flagged.
  2. Import active conversations so you keep the history in one place. Imported threads never receive automated steps.
  3. Pause the old tool before launching, so two tools never message the same people.
  4. Queue stale invitations for withdrawal, oldest first, at a few per day.
Honest fit

Who is Connectora not a good fit for?

Connectora is not the right tool if you need very high daily volume from each account, email and LinkedIn in one automated sequence, or InMail campaigns. It is built for teams that put account safety first and want every reply handled by a person.

We would rather tell you this on the page than on the demo. If one of these is a must-have, see how other tools compare on Compare.

  • Very high daily volume from each account
  • Email and LinkedIn in one automated sequence
  • InMail campaigns
